option_text: It describes one of the many reactive plans that are grouped under the NobleSocializing Playbook; hence, it is a local-level description.

When an agent meeting the TEMPER constraints and playing a role associated with NobleSocializing hears an insult, it either complains and lets the Regia "narrative layer" know that an insult has been thrown (if he is not drunk, and hates the host), or celebrates the host by  toasting him, otherwise.

When an agent playing a role that has been assigned the NobleSocializing Playbook hears an insult, it increases its priority to react to the insult by 5 units, it decreases its sympathy by 0.5 units, and it increases its aggressivennes by 0.2 units.

The plan has static priority 5 and can only be adopted by agents playing a role that has been assigned the NobleSocializing, and  whose sympathy is > -0.5; as a side effect of executing the plan, the agent's aggressivennes is increased by 0.2.

It describes a Plot, namely a narrative at a global level; the story is that once an insult is heard, every agent in the scenario who is not drunk and hates the host will complain; all the others will toast the host.
It describes one of the many reactive plans that are grouped under the RoyalBanquet Playbook; hence, it is a local-level description.

When an agent playing a role assigned the RoyalBanquet Playbook starts its execution cycle, it first enters a reception phase, then a feast phase, then a duel_interruption phase (in exactly this order); after the last phase is over, the agent may take one among the two Host and Guest roles.
It describes a Plot, namely a narrative at a global level.
It states that there are only two agents in the scenario, one named Host and one named Guest.

The RoyalBanquet plot starts in the reception phase, but from this fragment alone it is not possible to know which phase will come next: some TRANSITION TO statement inside a DURING block should drive phase transitions. The statements  ROLE Host. and ROLE Guest. declare that these two roles will be involved in this plot. From the fragment alone it is impossible to know which Playbook will be assigned to these roles, but it makes sense that some assignment, or some Role DO Action, will appear later in the Plot.
It describes what may happen during the PLOT phase, which is one of the phases designed by the Regia programmer.
It states that the attribute PRIORITY associated with the assassin becomes 9 when the assassin is spotted.
It states that this scenario involves one specific agent identified by the name WORLD, that is in charge for locking doors when the assassin is spotted.
It states that this scenario involves one specific agent identified by the name Host, that is in charge for calling guards when the doors are locked.

It states that whatever the current phase the Plot is in, when the assassin is spotted this block gains a very high priority (9); the world, namely some mechanism properly implemented in the environment (whatever the environment is; it might be a videogame, a multiagent system environment, a Virtual Reality environment) will ensure that doors are locked, while one agent playing the Host role will make sure to call guards. Then, the Plot ends.
